name: wcslib
desc: Library and utilities for the FITS World Coordinate System
why: Astronomy coordinate transform library for FITS images, real science you can run at home on sky data.

brief.what_it_is: WCSLIB is a C library, with FORTRAN wrapper functions, that implements the coordinate transformations defined in the FITS World Coordinate System papers. It works with the WCS keywords in a FITS image header and the coordinate systems they describe (celestial, spectral and time). The homepage lists several bundled utilities. HPXcvt converts 1D HEALPix pixelization data stored in FITS (ring or nested order in a binary table extension) into a 2D primary image array with HPX or XPH coordinate representation. The package also includes PGSBOX, a curvilinear axis drawing routine for PGPLOT that can optionally interface to WCSLIB. The homepage does not describe the other installed executables (fitshdr, sundazel, tofits, wcsware) beyond their names in the brew metadata.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as the reference implementation for the FITSWCS standard, which defines keywords and usage for describing astronomical coordinate systems in a FITS image header. WCSLIB is presented as a C implementation of the coordinate transformations those papers define.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internal mechanism. It says the library implements the transformations defined in the FITS WCS papers (Papers I to VII, including the HEALPix/HPX projection from Paper V and the XPH butterfly projection from Paper VI). It also points to a doxygen-generated programming manual in HTML and PDF, which I did not fetch.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation steps. It says WCSLIB is distributed as releases (the current one is 8.10, with older releases also available), and that the distribution includes RCS version files back to v1.0 from release 8.5 on. It also says test data is available: example FITS files for each projection in Paper II and for spectral representations from Paper III, plus a 13MiB bzip'd WMAP 3-year ILC map example for HPXcvt. Nothing on the page covers build requirements, accounts or runtime configuration.
brief.standout: It is the reference C implementation of the FITS WCS standard, which the homepage says was honoured with the 2025 ADASS software prize. It also ships a HEALPix-to-image converter (HPXcvt) and bundled test data for every projection in the standard, so you can check the transforms against known files.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage was last modified 2026-09-27, the same date as the announced WCSLIB 8.10 release with enhancements and bug fixes. The author's contact address is listed. The page's dates are as stated; I did not check a release page or repository commit history.
brief.caveats: Installation details, build requirements and the full list of commands are not on the homepage, so the brief does not cover them. The homepage is a literature and download page rather than a user guide. Based on the homepage, the library is C with FORTRAN wrappers, so it is aimed at people writing code, not at interactive use. The homepage gives no licence information. The brew description calls it a library for the FITS World Coordinate System, and the scout note calls it real science that can be run at home on sky data. The homepage does not say anything about running it that way.
quotes: WCSLIB is implemented in C, with support for FORTRAN via a set of wrapper functions.

Utility program HPXcvt is included with WCSLIB. It converts 1D HEALPix pixelization data stored in a variety of forms in FITS, including ring or nested organization in a binary table extension, into a 2D primary image array with HPX or XPH coordinate representation.
WCSLIB was honoured with the ADASS software prize for 2025 for which I gave the invited conference talk remotely by video.
